title: QCLI-447 review follow-ups: decision-record validation, forward-compat and contract drift (from #733)
description:
Non-blocking findings from the opus DEC-183 review of opum-ai/quest-cli#733 (the QCLI-447 decision-record widening, squash 7eb308595586fab0bff89ec5b8bf5c8db9506197). Filed so none of them is lost; each is one acceptance criterion below.

SEVERITY: (5) forward-compat and (6) CHANGELOG are HIGH - mixed quest versions run in this fleet, and the changelog is where a user learns the minimum version. The rest are medium or low at the worker judgement: (1) poor refusals and (2) untested validation are medium because they hide regressions; (3) id validation is medium; (7) the QCLI-266 repeatable-flag drift is medium because it already caused one divergence; (9) cleanup deleting a still-referenced decision is medium (data loss); (4), (8) and (10) are low.

The findings, verbatim in substance from the review: every schema refusal says "Invalid decision." without naming the field or the allowed values (src/domain/planning/planning.ts:105); unique() on adrs/supersedes (:107-108), source min(1) (:83), element min(1) (:86-87), the component: empty-repo regex (:61) and any edit-path refusal are untested and stay green if removed; supersedes/adrs ids are unvalidated (add a DEC-n format check and refuse self-reference, but NOT an existence check because DEC ids span trackers); the --source help text promises a vocabulary the code does not enforce (command-help.ts:552); an older quest that reads a rejected/withdrawn decision throws for the whole planning.json and an older quest doing ANY planning write strips the five new fields with no message (local-planning-repository.ts:54-57, :97-99) - name the minimum version; there is no CHANGELOG entry; command-parameters.ts:198/:223 claim the parser uses REPEATABLE_DECISION_FLAGS while main.ts:3072 inlines its own list (QCLI-266 drift; question ask at :3551 too); planning.ts:497 says three reported statuses when there are five; cleanup deletes a superseded decision a successor still points at; decision create/edit silently drop --task/--description (pre-existing, main.ts:3132-3135, 3244); and edit cannot clear a widened field or empty a list.

acceptanceCriteria.text: HIGH: An older quest reading a rejected or withdrawn decision no longer throws for the whole planning.json, AND an older quest doing any planning write no longer silently strips the five widened fields - either by tolerance or by a version gate - with the minimum compatible version named in the change
HIGH: CHANGELOG carries the entry naming the widened decision record and that minimum version
Every decision schema refusal names the field and the allowed values instead of Invalid decision. (src/domain/planning/planning.ts:105)
Tests cover the validation that currently stays green if removed: unique() on adrs/supersedes, source min(1), element min(1), the component: empty-repo regex, and the edit-path refusal
adrs and supersedes entries get a DEC-n format check and self-reference is refused; NO existence check is added, because DEC ids span trackers
The --source help text either enforces the vocabulary it promises or stops promising one (src/application/command-help.ts:552)
One source of truth for repeatable decision flags: command-parameters.ts no longer claims a list the parser does not use (main.ts:3072; question ask at :3551 has the same drift)
planning.ts:497 says five reported statuses, not three
cleanup no longer deletes a superseded decision that a successor still points at
decision create/edit stop silently dropping --task/--description (pre-existing, main.ts:3132-3135 and 3244)
decision edit can clear a widened field and empty a list, the gap the review named alongside the ten findings
